subject: Q4 Slate: owners' clearance & preflight checklist
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@monarch.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q4 Slate: owners' clearance & preflight checklist

Team — attaching the current Q4 OKR slate and the preflight runbook for the kickoff. This is the version I aligned with Product and Infra earlier this week; I need owners to confirm or flag changes by EOD today so we can lock the packet for the executive QBR on Monday.

Key asks:
- Owners: please confirm the KR targets you can commit to (inline) or indicate a revised target.
- Risks: if you have capacity or cross-team dependency risks, call them out now.
- Rollout: indicate whether the milestone requires a staged rollout (canary) or full release.

Highlights (quick):
- Objective A: Improve inference throughput and cost-efficiency — suggest a 15% token-cost reduction target (KR1).
- Objective B: Platform reliability — 99.95% p99 SLA target for hosted API.
- Objective C: Developer velocity — SDK adoption and onboarding metrics.

Attachments: Q4-OKR-Slate-v2.pdf, QBR-Preflight-Runbook.xlsx (deck & runbook stubs).
Link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2B_q4-okr-draft (live draft).

If I don't hear objections, I'll mark the slate as "prelim-approved" and circulate to Exec for visibility at 5pm PT.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
VP, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 Slate: owners' clearance & preflight checklist

Sean — thanks for the draft. Quick notes inline:
- Objective A / KR1: 15% cost reduction is fine as a target if we lock quantization profile changes to the dedicated pool. Otherwise I recommend 10% for hosted API only.
- Objective B: the 99.95% p99 SLA is achievable but we should scope the definition (global vs region-specific). Recommend we call out region scope in the KR text.
- Objective C: SDK adoption — change the metric to "active SDK consumers" rather than downloads.

I attached a 1-line change summary in the doc and left comments in the Google doc. No blocker from my side for prelim approval once the scope clarifications are added.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 Slate: owners' clearance & preflight checklist

+1 on Kim's notes. A couple of quick add-ins from Reliability:
- For the SLA KR, we need to include the measurement windows and the burn rate policy (what happens if we miss a quarterly target). I'll add a short paragraph in the runbook.
- Rollout: recommend a canary for Objective A KR2 (model compilation changes) — we shouldn't change quant profiles globally without a staged ramp.

I approve prelim sign-off assuming the SLA measurement text is added and we keep the canary plan in the runbook.

Hannah
Head of Reliability

Thanks — I reviewed the slate and the runbook. Approved from Growth's POV with two asks:
- Add a small KR under Objective C for "1 pilot customer deployed with SDK" by end of Q2 (helps show an adoption story for the QBR).
- For the rollout notes, please include a short rollback criteria item (so we can articulate guardrails to Sales/CS).

Otherwise happy to be an owner on Objective C and lead the pilot for the SDK deployment.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Growth
Redwood Inference

Sean — thanks. I reviewed latest comments in the doc and the runbook. TL;DR: prelim sign-off from Exec planning side.

Two operational asks I want tracked before we circulate to the full Exec:
1) Add the region scope to Objective B (per Kim) and call out whether the SLA is measured per-region and aggregated for the company metric.
2) Confirm burn rate / remediation steps in the runbook (Hannah will add this).

Assuming those two items are captured in the runbook, I approve prelim sign-off and greenlight you to share with Exec for visibility.

Jonas Weber
Chief of Staff, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
